interface.title: NeuroCarto (NPX - NeuroCarto), a Bokeh-based channel-map editor for Neuropixels probes
interface.stage_of_work: Planning an experiment before recording: deciding which electrodes are read out in a recording session
interface.what_it_is_for: Painting a desired recording-density pattern (a 'blueprint') onto a Neuropixels probe's electrodes and having the app build a channel map (.imro) that respects the probe's shared-channel hardware limits, while channel efficiency and density plots show how well the map matches the blueprint.

data.note: The Input file dropdown already listed example-NP24.imro (a 4-shank Neuropixels 2.0 map, 384/384 channels on the bottom of shank 0), plus bundled res/*.imro files including res/Fig3_example.imro, which comes with its blueprint and config. I also made a blank map with New > Neuropixels probe (NP1). Save writes files on the server, not as browser downloads. When the map uses all 384 channels it writes .imro, .blueprint.npy and .config.json. For an incomplete map it logs 'incomplete channelmap' and writes only .config.json and .blueprint.npy. Saved files appeared in the Input file list and could be loaded again.

features.name: Box-select on a layout figure + category/state paint buttons
features.general: Draw a box over items on a spatial layout, then press a labelled button to give every selected item that label or on/off state; the layout redraws with the new labels
features.specific: With the 'select electrode' box tool, drag over electrodes on the probe figure. Then press Full/Half/Quarter Density, Excluded, Pre Selected or Unset to set the blueprint, or Enable/Disable to change the channel map directly. A Low priority button also exists, but applying it showed no visible effect and it has no legend colour, so what it does is unconfirmed
steps: activate the box-select tool in the plot toolbar
drag a rectangle over electrodes on one or more shanks
press a category button (Full Density, Excluded, …) or a state button (Enable/Disable)
watch the coloured blueprint bar beside the shank, or the green/black electrodes, update
serves_tasks: Mark a region of sites as needed at full coverage
Mark other regions at lower coverage levels
Keep certain sites from ever being used
Adjust individual sites by hand, as a manual alternative or a follow-up to the automatic result
Force specific sites to be kept whatever the automatic choice

features.name: Constraint-solving auto-selection with Auto/Refresh modes
features.general: Turn a desired-priority map into a valid assignment under a hardware budget, either live after every edit or only when asked
features.specific: Auto (toggle) rebuilds the channel map from the blueprint after every category change; with Auto off, Refresh rebuilds it on demand. The solver respects the 384-channel limit and shared-channel conflicts, keeps Pre Selected electrodes, and drops manual Enable/Disable picks. Refresh also resets the reference to External. A valid, saveable map uses all 384 channels. With heavy exclusion the solver may fill fewer (e.g. 374/384), and Save will then not write the .imro
steps: paint a blueprint
keep Auto on for live updates, or turn it off
press Refresh to recompute
read the new map (green electrodes) and check the per-shank and total channel counts reach 384
serves_tasks: Force specific sites to be kept whatever the automatic choice

features.name: Blueprint overlay with legend and conflict view
features.general: Show the requested design as coloured bands beside the layout, with a switch that recolours the parts the result fails to meet, and a switch to hide the bands
features.specific: The Blueprint switch draws green/orange/blue/pink bars (full, half, quarter, excluded) next to each shank and can be switched off to declutter. Ticking Conflict replaces them with red where the channel map does not satisfy the blueprint
steps: switch Blueprint on
read the category bars against the legend
tick Conflict to show unmet areas in red
untick to go back
switch Blueprint off to hide the bars
serves_tasks: See where the requested design could not be met

features.name: Live efficiency statistics panel
features.general: A summary table that recomputes resources used vs. requested and an efficiency percentage every time the design or assignment changes
features.specific: The Channel Efficiency panel shows used channels (total and per shank s0–s3), request electrodes and channel efficiency %
steps: edit the blueprint or the selection
read used channels per shank
compare requested electrodes with the 384 available
use the efficiency % to decide whether to trim the blueprint
serves_tasks: Check how much of the requested coverage the hardware delivers
Shrink a requested region that asks for more sites than the hardware can read

features.name: Per-shank density curve overlay
features.general: Draw a profile curve beside each column of the layout showing how dense the selected items are along depth
features.specific: The Electrode Density Curve switch draws a blue density trace beside each shank for the current channel map
steps: switch Electrode Density Curve on
regenerate the map
compare curve peaks with the blueprint bars
switch off to declutter, and on again to restore
serves_tasks: Check how much of the requested coverage the hardware delivers

features.name: Probe figure navigation with hover info
features.general: Pan, wheel-zoom, axis-locked wheel-pan and reset a spatial layout plot, with a hover tooltip identifying each item
features.specific: Bokeh toolbar: Pan, Wheel Zoom, Wheel Pan (y-axis), Reset, and 'electrode information' hover showing Channel and (x,y) (e.g. Channel 364/366 on shank 2)
steps: choose Pan or Wheel Zoom and move around the probe
switch to Wheel Pan to scroll along depth
hover an electrode to read its channel and position
press Reset to return to the full view
serves_tasks: Check how much of the requested coverage the hardware delivers
See where the requested design could not be met

features.name: Project file I/O: open, new, and save a bundle
features.general: Pick a file from a server-side list or start a new document of a chosen type, then save it under a name as a bundle of related files that reload together; the full bundle is written only when the document passes a completeness check
features.specific: Input file dropdown + Load; New menu (4-Shank NP2.0 variants, NP2.0, NP1); Save filename + Save. When the map uses all channels (384/384), Save writes .imro, .blueprint.npy and .config.json. An incomplete map logs 'incomplete channelmap' and writes only .config.json and .blueprint.npy. Load restores whichever of the three exist and auto-suggests an incremented save name. A clear button empties the Log
steps: pick a file in Input file and press Load, or pick a probe type from New
edit until the map uses all channels
type a Save filename
press Save and check the log for 'save channelmap' (or 'incomplete channelmap')
reload the saved file from Input file
